text:
jordan: Quick sync — noticed repeated short bursts from a few Dedicated tenants that are hammering cold-start latency and spiking cost. thinking we should decouple prewarm budget from admission ledger and introduce a short adaptive warmup window. thoughts?

maya: can you paste an example burst trace? is this > 95th percentile or legit traffic spikes?

jordan: here — 2 tenants, platinum & gold. bursts: 90s windows, qps spike 6x, median provision_time ~22s. tail p95 latency climbs to 3.8s. observed repeated warmups every ~5m.

hao: ugh that provisioning time kills small RLHF calls. decoupling sounds ok but we need a safety cap so plating doesn't starve other tenants. proposal: 1) short warmup window (W) that pre-allocs ephemeral GPUs for recent bursty tenants; 2) charge the tenant for prewarm tokens but at discounted rate; 3) if cluster capacity low, fall back to queued admission.

lucas: agree on discounting — otherwise tenants will never accept prewarm cost. how do we compute W? naive fixed value is brittle.

jordan: adaptive idea: W = min(max_window, observed_burst_tail * multiplier). small sketch: effective_headroom = max(min_reserved, peak_1m * factor_by_sla) - in_flight. factor_by_sla {silver:1.2,gold:1.5,platinum:2.0}. if effective_headroom > threshold -> prewarm for tenant for W seconds.

sam: two operational concerns: a) accounting lines must show prewarm charge separately in console; b) need kill-switch by region in case a tenant goes rogue.

hao: also: separate admission token pool for warmups vs steady requests so steady traffic doesn't get evicted by short-lived prewarms. token-banking for steady, ephemeral pool for warmups. tokens should be reconciled in billing once warmup used or released.

lucas: operator-surface question: should the dedicated operator expose a WarmupIntent CRD or keep it internal to the controller? WarmupIntent gives product visibility and manual overrides.

jordan: leaning WarmupIntent CRD + operator default controller. CRD fields: tenant_id, requested_headroom, ttl_seconds, cost_estimate. sample: ```apiVersion: orch.redwood/v1
kind: WarmupIntent
metadata:
  name: warmup-tenant-42
spec:
  tenant: tenant-42
  headroom: 2   # GPUs
  ttlSeconds: 90
  priority: gold
```

maya: nice. also add reason field and a fingerprint of recent bursts. makes audits easier.

orch-bot: deploy-check: warmup-intent schema validated against operator v2.3.1. if you change fields run `make operator-bindings`

hao: rollout plan idea: 1) implement controller-side warmup pool + metric (warmup_allocations_total), 2) expose CRD but default controller auto-creates intents, 3) UI show prewarm cost, 4) A/B test with selective tenants.

sam: fallback policy: if cluster at >85% util, warmups should be throttled by priority and by a burst-frequency penalty. i.e., repeated warmups in short time increase cost multiplier and reduce W.

jordan: question for design: do we let warmups preempt preemptible jobs? my vote: yes but only preemptible and only if tenant SLA >= gold and only up to a soft cap per region.

lucas: agree. need to update eviction docs and pack a k8s preemption annotation on nodes hosting preemptible jobs. also add alert `warmup-preemptions > 0` to eng-oncall.

maya: small nit: when calculating headroom use smoothed peak (exponential window) to avoid reacting to single-runaway spikes. smoothing tau ~60s.

jordan: action items: 1) hao proto CRD PR w/ schema + validation; 2) lucas update operator eviction docs + alert; 3) maya console mockups for prewarm billing; 4) sam add region kill-switch + runbook. assigning owners in GH now.

hao: will open PR with CRD and controller sketch tomorrow AM.

lucas: I'll draft eviction doc and k8s annotation.

maya: I'll attach console mocks to the PR — need wiring for cost signals.

sam: I'll write runbook + region toggle and add to release checklist.

jordan: thanks all — if nobody objects i'll turn this into a short RFC after PRs land. :thumbsup:
